newsitem.title: USA: United Healthcare up on perceived recovery.
newsitem.headline: United Healthcare up on perceived recovery.

text.p: Shares in United Healthcare Corp rose 4-1/4 to 44-1/4 Thursday on Wall Street perceptions that the largest U.S. managed care firm is on the mend.

The Minneapolis-based HMO giant reported third-quarter profits below the year-ago level, as expected. But analysts pointed to sequential improvement over the second quarter, strong enrollment growth and an improved 1997 outlook.
"The worst is over," said Dean Witter healthcare industry analyst Todd Richter.
Managed healthcare stocks gained ground on Wednesday in the wake of the national elections.
That helped buoy United Healthcare again on Thursday, said Goldman Sachs analyst Roberta Walter.
She added, however, that United's third-quarter results indicate that "1997 will be a substantially better year."
The company reported total revenues for the third quarter ended September 30, 1996, of $2.59 billion, up from $1.22 billion for the same period a year ago.

Third quarter profits were $91.2 million, or $0.45 per share, in line with Wall Street expectations. They were up from $0.43 per share in the second quarter of 1996, but down from $0.53 per share a year ago.
